results.title: a core set of principles for data access within trusted research ...
results.content: These principles provide the foundation for a standardised UK TRE DAA template, designed to support the growing ecosystem of TREs. By providing a familiar structure and terms, this template aims to build trust among data owners and the UK public and to provide clarity to researchers on their obligations to protect the data. The UK Health Data Research Alliance [16], an independent alliance of leading healthcare and research organisations united to establish best practice for the ethical use of UK health data for research at scale, commits members to using a proportionate governance approach to data access based on the ‘Five Safes framework’ [17] via its principles for participation [18]. The Pan-UK Data Governance Steering Group, a working group of the UK Health Data Research Alliance, has developed a set of core principles of data access for research in TREs, to underpin a template DAA.

results.content: Together, consent tracking and data use monitoring could not only enhance privacy but also foster trust in healthcare and research by assuring individuals that their information is securely and responsibly managed and its sharing provides real societal value. Several technologies could enable the tracking of health data use, data sharing consent, and reporting information of subsequent PG-HD uses to individuals. **Table 2 Overview of the three technologies Blockchain, Self-sovereign identity/Decentralized identifiers (SSI/DIDs) and De-identified tokens on how they can be used in tracking of health data and data sharing consent**. For instance, MIT’s MedRec51 25–30 (2016).") used Ethereum to manage access to electronic medical records, while the EU-funded MyHealthMyData52.") project tested blockchain-based consent mechanisms for sharing health data. Blockchain with SSI/DIDs supports personalized consent and accountability, while de-identified tokens enable secure linkage across institutional silos, together facilitating privacy-preserving, interoperable health data ecosystems. Emerging technologies like blockchain, SSI, DIDs, and de-identified tokens offer innovative solutions to modernize tracking of health data use and consent and enhance transparency (Fig. 4).
